title: HieraticBench exposes a blind spot in reading ancient handwriting
friendlyTitle: Leading AI models could not read one hieratic sentence
summary: HieraticBench reports that 13 tested model families failed to identify or correctly translate a modern sample written in hieratic, the everyday handwriting of ancient Egypt. The project publishes model responses, invites Egyptologists to contribute sealed examples and provides a harness for repeatable model tests.
friendlySummary: A benchmark gave AI models a sentence written in an ancient Egyptian handwriting style. None of the tested models correctly identified and translated it.
whyItMatters: Broad visual-language ability can conceal severe gaps in specialist scripts and low-resource domains. Archives, museums and researchers should benchmark models on representative expert-verified material before using them to transcribe or translate collections—and retain uncertainty rather than rewarding confident guesses.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI can look capable but still fail badly on rare writing systems. Experts need to test it with real examples before trusting it with historical records.
